---
title: "Bonds — Review"
---

## Essential Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|-------|-----------|
| **Bond** (Bond) | Debt instrument : issuer borrows, investor lends |
| **Coupon** (Coupon) | Fixed periodic payment = lender's reward |
| **Principal** (Face Value) | Amount repaid at maturity |
| **Maturity** (Maturity) | Date of principal repayment |
| **Yield** (Yield) $y$ | Rate of return required by the investor |
| **Default Risk** (Default Risk) | Risk of partial or total non-repayment |
| **Credit Spread** | $y_{\text{corporate}} - y_{\text{sovereign}}$ |
| **Zero-coupon** (Zero Coupon) | Bond without coupon, sold below par |

---

## Price Formula (key !)

$$\boxed{B(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i \cdot e^{-y(t_i - t)} + P \cdot e^{-y(T-t)}}$$

- $c_i$ : coupon at $t_i$ — $P$ : principal — $y$ : yield — $T$ : maturity

::: {.callout-important title="Price ↔ yield relation"}
**Inverse and convex** : $y \uparrow \Rightarrow B \downarrow$ and $y \downarrow \Rightarrow B \uparrow$
:::

---

## Price vs Face Value

| Situation | Condition | Cause |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| **Premium** (Premium) | $B > 100$ | Coupon > market rate |
| **At Par** (At Par) | $B = 100$ | Coupon = market rate |
| **Discount** (Discount) | $B < 100$ | Coupon < market rate |

---

## Quick Numerical Example

> Bond : $c = 5$ CHF × 4 payments, $P = 100$, $y = 5\%$

| Cash Flow | Present Value |
|------|----------------|
| $c_1$ at $t=0.5$ | $5 \cdot e^{-0.05 \times 0.5} = 4.88$ |
| $c_2$ at $t=1.0$ | $5 \cdot e^{-0.05 \times 1.0} = 4.76$ |
| $c_3$ at $t=1.5$ | $5 \cdot e^{-0.05 \times 1.5} = 4.64$ |
| $c_4$ at $t=2.0$ | $5 \cdot e^{-0.05 \times 2.0} = 4.52$ |
| $P$ at $t=2.0$ | $100 \cdot e^{-0.05 \times 2.0} = 90.48$ |
| **Total** | **$B = 109.28$ → at premium** |

## Trial & Error Procedure

**Objective** : find $y$ knowing $B$ (inverse problem, no analytical solution).

**Residual** :

$$\text{residual}(y) = B_{\text{observed}} - B_{\text{calculated}}(y)$$

**Algorithm** :

1. Start from very high $y$ ($y = 100$)
2. Residual > 0 → $y \leftarrow y/2$
3. Residual < 0 → $y \leftarrow (y_{\text{previous}} + y)/2$
4. Repeat until $|\text{residual}| < 10^{-3}$

---

## Zero-Coupon Yield Curve (Bootstrap)

**Why ?** Bonds with different coupons are not comparable → zero-coupon standard.

**Bootstrap — logic** : extract zero rates one by one, from shortest to longest.

### Formulas by case

**Short-term zero-coupon** (0.25 year) :

$$r_{0.25} = 4 \cdot \ln\!\left(1 + \frac{\text{quarterly gain}}{4}\right)$$

**1-year zero-coupon** :

$$r_{1.0} = \ln\!\left(1 + \frac{P - B}{B}\right)$$

**With coupons** (1.5 year) : isolate $r_{1.5}$ in :

$$\sum_i c_i \cdot e^{-r_{t_i} \cdot t_i} + (P + c_{\text{last}}) \cdot e^{-r_{1.5} \cdot 1.5} = B$$

### Example result

| Maturity (years) | $r$ (%) |
|---------------|---------|
| 0.25 | 10.127 |
| 0.50 | 10.469 |
| 1.0 | 10.536 |
| 1.5 | 10.681 |
| 2.0 | 10.808 |

## Types of Bonds

```{mermaid}
graph TD
    A[Bonds] --> B[Government / Sovereign\nGovies / Treasuries]
    A --> C[Corporates\nCorporate Bonds]
    B --> D[Best rating AAA\nLowest yield]
    C --> E[Investment Grade BBB+\nModerate spread]
    C --> F[High Yield / Junk BB-\nHigh spread]
```

**Agencies** : S&P (AAA → D) | Moody's (Aaa → C) | Fitch (AAA → D)

::: {.callout-note title="Key formula"}
$y_{\text{corporate}} = y_{\text{sovereign}} + \text{Credit Spread}$
:::

## 5 Bond Risks

| Risk | Mechanism | Protection |
|--------|-----------|------------|
| **Interest Rate** (Interest Rate) | $y \uparrow \Rightarrow B \downarrow$ | Short duration |
| **Credit** (Credit) | Issuer default | High rating |
| **Inflation** (Inflation) | Purchasing power erosion : $r_{\text{real}} = r_{\text{nom}} - \pi$ | TIPS, gold |
| **Liquidity** (Liquidity) | Sale at discounted price | Liquid bonds |
| **Reinvestment** (Reinvestment) | Coupons reinvested at lower rates | Avoid callables |

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall — Callable Bonds"}
If rates fall → issuer calls the bond → forced reinvestment at lower rates.
:::

---

## Role in a Portfolio

| Role | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Diversification** | Negative correlation with equities (except 2022 !) |
| **Income** | Regular and predictable coupons |
| **Capital preservation** | Principal guaranteed at maturity (if no default) |
| **Strategic allocation** | Increasing share with age (life-cycle investing) |

::: {.callout-important title="2022 Exception"}
Brutal rate hike → bonds **and** equities down simultaneously → **positive** correlation.
:::

## Revision Checklist

- [ ] I can calculate $B(t)$ from $y$, $c_i$, $P$, $T$
- [ ] I can interpret premium / discount / at par
- [ ] I understand the Trial & Error algorithm (search direction)
- [ ] I can apply Bootstrap on a coupon-bearing example
- [ ] I know the 5 risks and their protections
- [ ] I know that $y_{\text{corp}} = y_{\text{gov}} + \text{spread}$
- [ ] I understand why 2022 broke diversification
